heroHeadline: Trump-Xi Summit 'Meagre' (May 15): 200 Boeing Jets, No Iran Deal, No H200 Resolution; S&P 500 -0.9%; Warsh Officially Assumes Fed Chair; April Retail Sales +4.9% YoY; Section 122 Cliff July 23 (68 Days)
heroSubtitle: The Trump-Xi Beijing summit concluded May 15 with outcomes analysts described as 'meagre' — falling far short of pre-summit expectations. Concrete deliverables: China ordered 200 Boeing jets (vs. ~500 anticipated — Boeing shares fell ~4%); agricultural purchases in 'double-digit billions' (no volume specified); China agreed to buy US oil (no volume); rare earth mutual de-escalation (Trump dropped 100% tariff threat; China paused export restrictions — but no formal deal signed); Board of Trade framework for ~$30B tariff reduction from each side (not yet implemented). Critical gaps: President Trump did not ask Xi for help with the Strait of Hormuz blockade (per Sec. Rubio) — Brent crude remains ~$105-110/bbl, sustaining the energy shock that drove April CPI to 3.8% and PPI to 6.0%. No definitive H200 Nvidia chip deal. Xi called the summit 'landmark'; Trump invited Xi for a September Washington visit; two more face-to-faces scheduled. Market reaction (May 15): S&P 500 -0.9%, Nasdaq -1.3%, Dow -407pts (-0.8%) — Wall Street saw 'nothing of real substance.' Kevin Warsh officially became the 17th Federal Reserve Chair on May 15 as Powell's term expired; his first FOMC is June 16-17. Counter-balancing: April Retail Sales +0.5% MoM (+4.9% YoY) confirm consumer resilience despite record-low sentiment (Michigan 47.6); Empire State Manufacturing 19.6 — highest since early 2022. ECB increasingly expected to hike twice in 2026 (Bloomberg survey May 11). Stagflation backdrop: CPI 3.8%, PPI 6.0%, core PCE 3.2%, CME hike odds ~30%, 10Y yield ~4.49%. Section 122 tariff cliff: July 23 (68 days). Recession probabilities: Goldman ~20%, JPMorgan ~35%, Moody's ~40%.
